title: Componentwise normalization: local structure and birational recognition
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], and write $
u_X:X^
u	o X$ for the componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. (1) $X^
u$ is normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and $
u_X$ is integral and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. It induces a bijection of generic points of irreducible components; for each such point $\eta\in X$, the fibre $X^
u	imes_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ over $\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-fibre-product]. (2) For every open subscheme $U\subseteq X$, the restriction $(X^
u)	imes_X U	o U$ is canonically its componentwise normalization; if $U$ is normal this restriction is an isomorphism. (3) Let $Z$ be a normal locally Noetherian scheme and $f:Z	o X$ an integral morphism. Suppose $f$ induces a bijection between the generic points of irreducible components, and for every generic point $\xi\in Z$ with image $\eta$ the induced residue-field map $\kappa(\eta)	o\kappa(\xi)$ is an isomorphism. Then there is a unique isomorphism $Z\cong X^
u$ over $X$. The empty scheme and nonreduced $X$ are allowed.

source.place: Tags 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), parts (1)--(3), including the footnote allowing birationality on reductions; 035K (lemma-normalization-localization); 0H7D (lemma-normalization-trivial). Generic fibre statement from the construction in equation-generic-points and Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization). Recognition in (3) is 035Q(3) followed by 0H7D on Z.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties] to $X$. Its hypothesis is precisely local Noetherianity, with no reducedness or excellence requirement. Its conclusion gives every assertion in (1), including normality as integrally closed domain stalks and the canonical isomorphism of the entire generic fibre with the residue-field spectrum. In particular this is a scheme-fibre assertion, not merely a bijection of its points.

Let $U\subseteq X$ be any open subscheme. The open-subscheme assertion in [pqf-def-locnoeth] gives local Noetherianity of $U$ and of each open subscheme of $U$ or $X$. Any quasi-compact such open is therefore Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives finitely many irreducible components. Thus both $X$ and $U$ satisfy the quasi-compact-open finiteness hypothesis of the normalization chart and triviality lemmas used below. This reasoning does not assume that $U$ itself is quasi-compact.

source.place: Hypotheses of Tags 035P (lemma-description-normalization) and 0H7D (lemma-normalization-trivial); Properties Tag 01OV and Morphisms Tag 01T6.

proof.text:
Put $N=X^
u	imes_XU$; by the base-change assertion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] this is the open inverse image of $U$ in $X^
u$. For each affine open $V\subseteq U$, also affine in $X$, apply [lem-sfb-normalization-generic-residue-affine-charts] to $X$ and to $U$. Write $A_V=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. In both applications the index set is the generic points of $V$ and the ring is the integral closure $D_V$ of $A_V$ in the product of their residue fields. The ambient stalks are unchanged on open restriction: neighbourhoods contained in the open are cofinal among neighbourhoods of a point, so their stalk colimits, residue quotients and germ maps coincide. Consequently the two rings $D_V$, their $A_V$-algebra maps, and the charts $N	imes_UV\simeq\operatorname{Spec}D_V\simeq U^
u	imes_UV$ agree canonically. The compatibility clause of the cited chart lemma identifies restriction maps for every affine inclusion $W\subseteq V$, in both applications, with the same projection on generic residue-field factors. Hence these chart isomorphisms and their inverses agree on affine opens in overlaps. Such affine opens cover every overlap, without requiring the overlaps themselves affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] the local maps glue in both directions, and the composites are identities since they are identities on each chart. This constructs the canonical isomorphism $N\simeq U^
u$ over $U$ required by the first assertion of (2).

source.place: Tag 035K (lemma-normalization-localization), via the affine construction of Tag 035P and the componentwise identification Tag 0CDV. The chart compatibility spells out the localization implicit in 035K.

proof.text:
If $U$ is normal, step 2 verifies the finite-component hypothesis of [lem-sfb-normalization-normal-locally-finite]. That lemma makes $
u_U:U^
u	o U$ an isomorphism. Compose the isomorphism of step 3 with $
u_U$; because step 3 is over $U$, this composite is exactly the restriction $N	o U$. This proves the second assertion of (2). For $U=\varnothing$, every chart, inverse image and normalization in steps 2--4 is empty, and the glued maps are the unique maps of empty schemes.

For (3), apply [lem-sfb-integral-normal-generic-recognition] with $T=X$ and $a=f:Z\to X$. Its target is locally Noetherian by assumption; its source has integrally closed domain stalks because $Z$ is normal. Its remaining hypotheses are exactly the assumed integrality of $f$, bijection of component-generic points and residue-field isomorphisms. It concludes a unique isomorphism $Z\xrightarrow{\sim}X^\nu$ over $X$. This lemma even allows a source not locally Noetherian, so the stated stronger source hypothesis causes no gap. It explicitly permits nonreduced $X$ and the empty schemes. Thus (3) follows with its uniqueness clause, without assuming that generic stalks of nonreduced $X$ are fields.

lean.statement: theorem componentwiseNormalization_properties (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] : ((∀ x : X.reducedNormalization, IsDomain (X.reducedNormalization.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.reducedNormalization.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ IsIntegralHom X.fromReducedNormalization ∧ Surjective X.fromReducedNormalization ∧ Set.BijOn X.fromReducedNormalization {x : X.reducedNormalization | ∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X.reducedNormalization, IsGenericPoint x C} {x : X | ∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, IsGenericPoint x C} ∧ (∀ η : X, (∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, IsGenericPoint η C) → IsIso (pullback.snd X.fromReducedNormalization (X.fromSpecResidueField η)))) ∧ (∀ U : X.Opens, (∃! e : pullback X.fromReducedNormalization U.ι ≅ U.toScheme.reducedNormalization, e.hom ≫ U.toScheme.fromReducedNormalization = pullback.snd X.fromReducedNormalization U.ι) ∧ ((∀ x : U.toScheme, IsDomain (U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk x)) → IsIso (pullback.snd X.fromReducedNormalization U.ι))) ∧ (∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsLocallyNoetherian Z) (f : Z ⟶ X) (_ : IsIntegralHom f), (∀ z : Z, IsDomain (Z.presheaf.stalk z) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Z.presheaf.stalk z)) → Set.BijOn f {z : Z | ∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, IsGenericPoint z C} {x : X | ∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, IsGenericPoint x C} → (∀ z : Z, (∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, IsGenericPoint z C) → IsIso (f.residueFieldMap z)) → ∃! e : Z ≅ X.reducedNormalization, e.hom ≫ X.fromReducedNormalization = f)
